note: Single source of truth for the pi-web merge boundary. `driftedUpstreamFiles` lists files agegr/pi-web owns that this fork has also edited — every one is a potential merge conflict, and a potential SILENT semantic conflict when git merges cleanly but the two sides changed different things. The automated sync (.github/workflows/component-updates.yml) intersects each incoming upstream release with this map to decide whether it may push to main unattended. Human-facing rationale lives in docs/ownership-boundaries.md.

riskModel.note: Risk follows STRUCTURAL drift, not total drift. Replacing an upstream inline style object with a className produces a large diff, but an upstream edit to the same line conflicts textually and fails the sync loudly — that is safe. Rewritten JSX trees and code moved across files are what merge cleanly while being wrong. components/ModelsConfig.tsx is the reference: 146 changed lines, only 12 structural, correctly rated low. Recompute with the hunk classifier described in docs/ownership-boundaries.md after any significant change to a shared file.

autoPushPolicy.note: Risk levels that force the sync to open a reviewed PR instead of pushing straight to main and triggering a signed release. Most upstream releases will land here, because the remaining drift is accepted by decision rather than pending cleanup — see `dispositions` and `decisionLog`. Narrow this list only if the drift itself actually goes away.

lib/pi-sdk-internals.ts.reason: The locked SDK adapter wraps default MCP OAuth storage with the app's encrypted backend and versions the hot-reload cache. Constructor options and refresh-lock behavior must survive upstream updates.

lib/mcp-config-read.ts.reason: OAuth status is derived from a readonly encrypted store snapshot, without creating credential files, migrating records or returning token values to the renderer.

lib/mcp-sign-in.ts.reason: Sign-out selects the encrypted Pilaude state file and backend while retaining the original late-refresh and cancelled-sign-in write guards.

lib/builtin-extensions.ts.reason: The actual MCP extension is explicitly given encrypted credentials so its internal default cannot silently restore SDK plaintext token storage.

instrumentation.ts.reason: Initialize the independent Pilaude agent directory before importing any SDK-backed instrumentation or creating background services.

instrumentation-node.ts.reason: Server shutdown stream listeners are replaced by their owned Symbol during hot reload rather than accumulating one listener per registration.

components/SettingsPanel.tsx.reason: Pilaude mounts its app-owned data import section beside the existing desktop update section. Preserve this mount and existing settings behavior when merging upstream.

components/ModelsConfig.tsx.reason: Encrypted custom-provider credentials stay outside models.json and the generic account list. Saved request headers render empty masked inputs with opaque references; upstream changes must preserve both account membership and secret editing semantics.

components/DirectoryPicker.tsx.reason: Directory navigation ignores obsolete async responses and blocks selection during loading. An upstream merge must retain these protections against selecting a stale folder.

lib/model-runtime.ts.reason: Runtime construction delegates to the Pilaude encrypted credential adapter while keeping Pi's extension provider setup and network options.

lib/model-discovery-auth.ts.reason: Provider discovery composes its draft through the Pilaude transient runtime so literal API keys and request headers are never written to temporary models configuration.

lib/provider-credential-store.ts.reason: Production provider save/delete calls use encrypted Pilaude storage; the explicit legacy authPath adapter remains available to upstream tests and CLI consumers.

lib/provider-usage.ts.reason: Provider usage requests construct the same encrypted-credential model runtime as normal agent requests, avoiding a fallback to the SDK plaintext auth store.

lib/subagent-runtime.ts.reason: Subagent fallback runtime construction uses Pilaude credentials. Keep this adapter when updating upstream subagent lifecycle or runtime sharing.

app/api/models/route.ts.reason: The models listing supplies the Pilaude encrypted runtime factory to Pi's session services; removing it silently restores plaintext SDK authentication.

app/api/models/default/route.ts.reason: Saving a default model must use the same encrypted credential runtime as the model list so DPAPI-backed providers remain available to the selector star.

app/api/models-config/route.ts.reason: Saving custom providers moves literal keys and all nonempty request headers to DPAPI stores, checks request origin and publishes sanitized models.json under paired writer locks. Errors must not reflect secret input.

app/api/models-config/test/route.ts.reason: Model probes use transient Pilaude authentication without secret temporary files. Resolved keys and headers must be redacted from both diagnostic responses and errors before truncation.

app/api/models-config/discover/route.ts.reason: Discovery validates origin and JSON before network access, resolves encrypted request headers and redacts upstream failures with the actual request credentials. Upstream changes must retain these boundaries.

lib/models-config-store.ts.reason: Invalid model configuration errors preserve the source file and omit parser excerpts, which can contain literal request credentials from older configuration.

lib/models-config-redaction.ts.reason: This post-baseline upstream helper now replaces request headers with scoped legacy or encrypted references before API responses. Preserve literal API key masking and hidden-header round trips together. Drift is measured against origin/main because the file did not exist at the pi-web baseline.

lib/i18n/messages/en.ts.reason: Pilaude welcome, branding, and explicit local data migration messages extend the upstream locale. Preserve the complete matching locale key sets when merging.

lib/i18n/messages/zh-CN.ts.reason: Pilaude welcome, branding, and explicit local data migration messages extend the upstream locale. Preserve the complete matching locale key sets when merging.

lib/i18n/messages/zh-TW.ts.reason: Pilaude welcome, branding, and explicit local data migration messages extend the upstream locale. Preserve the complete matching locale key sets when merging.

components/SessionSidebar.tsx.reason: ~500 lines were MOVED OUT into components/ProjectPicker.tsx and components/path-ui.tsx, which do not exist upstream. git merge does not track cross-file moves: an upstream edit to the project-picker block can merge back cleanly and silently resurrect a second copy.

components/AppShell.tsx.reason: The author 0.7.3 shell extraction and Pilaude navigation, desktop chrome and measured Context coexistence differ from the recorded baseline. Preserve high-risk upstream merge review for the interaction and focus boundaries.

components/FileViewer.tsx.reason: Native file toolbar and panel adaptations still differ from the recorded pi-web baseline. Removing unused FileViewerStatus did not remove the shared-file drift; retain upstream merge review.

components/FileExplorer.tsx.reason: Took upstream FileExplorer wholesale in the v0.8.11 merge (its file-search implementation won); only the selectedFilePath prop remains fork-side. Kept deliberately.

components/TabBar.tsx.reason: Accessibility work plus the terminal-tab affordance: role="tab", aria-selected, roving tabIndex, keyboard activation, and a New terminal button. The terminal action is fork interaction design inside an upstream-owned component, so incoming TabBar changes require review.

components/ChatWindow.tsx.reason: Redesigned empty state — the new-session branding header (app icon + PRODUCT_NAME) is removed and only the update chip remains. Part of the fork's interaction design. Kept deliberately.

hooks/useTheme.ts.reason: Follows the OS colour scheme until the user picks a theme explicitly, and drops the ToggleOrigin argument so the view transition always starts from the centre. The view transition itself is unchanged from upstream. Kept deliberately.

hooks/useChatAppearance.ts.reason: The Windows reference uses a 16px default reading size. Preserve the existing stored user preference and width/font reset behavior when merging.

e2e/chat-appearance.mjs.reason: Appearance reset assertions track the 16px Windows default; persistence, independent width/font reset and multiline resizing assertions remain unchanged. Drift is measured against origin/main because this file postdates the baseline.

components/ChatInput.tsx.reason: Composer chrome restyle. Upstream changed this file in v0.8.1, and components/ChatInput.test.mjs covers it.

lib/i18n/registry.ts.reason: Relative imports of ./messages/en and ./messages/zh-CN carry explicit .ts extensions so lib/i18n/registry.test.mjs can load the file through Node's native type stripping (same constraint that put allowImportingTsExtensions in tsconfig.json). Two import lines; conflicts here would be textual.

next.config.ts.reason: Desktop standalone build branch. Also holds serverExternalPackages, which upstream updates whenever it adds a pi package — do NOT auto-derive that list here.

app/layout.tsx.reason: native-theme.css import, branding title, dark-mode bootstrap script.

eslint.config.mjs.reason: Adds ignores for the desktop build output directories.

lib/rpc-manager.ts.reason: Pilaude session services must retain the encrypted-credential runtime factory together with the fork's event and session lifecycle behavior during upstream merges.

components/BranchNavigator.tsx.reason: className hook only, no structural change — the intended shape for every restyled file.

package.json.reason: Desktop scripts and Tauri deps. Name stays @agegr/pi-web on purpose — see docs/ownership-boundaries.md.

tsconfig.json.reason: resolveJsonModule for branding, plus allowImportingTsExtensions: lib/*.test.mjs load .ts sources through Node's native type stripping, which requires explicit extensions on relative imports.

.gitignore.reason: Desktop build output plus local agent tooling state (.claude/, .spec-workflow/).

dispositions.accepted: Reviewed and kept. The drift is either the fork's own interaction design or a generic improvement with no desktop coupling, so it cannot be extracted into components/desktop/. Removing it would mean deleting a feature. These files stay permanent review points; that is the running cost of a UI fork, not a backlog item. Do not reopen without new information.
dispositions.reduce: Drift that can be removed without losing anything — desktop-only code that belongs in components/desktop/, or fork additions sitting in an upstream file that can move to a fork-owned one. Act on these.
